swing/unit: A unit adds up its inputs, each times its weight, into one number, z. A new example brings new inputs, and a new z.
swing/one: Say each term, an input times its weight, is minus one or one, at random. With one term, z is just that.
swing/four: Four such terms, and z can land as far as four out on either side, though most often near zero.
swing/many: A hundred, and z swings far wider: it often lands ten or more from zero.
swing/flat: That matters for the bend that comes next: far from zero the tan-aitch is flat, so a z out there leaves the unit saturated.
spread/mean: Take the simplest swing: minus two or two, equally often. Its mean, the average, is zero: the center of the swing.
spread/dev: Each value lies two away from the mean, one on each side. That gap, the value minus the mean, is its deviation.
spread/var: Square each deviation, and average: four and four average to four. That average squared deviation is the variance.
spread/std: The square root of four is two, back in the value's own units: the standard deviation, the size of a typical deviation.
spread/name: Karl Pearson gave it that name in 1894. Code writes it S T D.
adds/pair: Now add two values, each minus one or one, so each has a variance of one.
adds/indep: Say they are independent: one tells you nothing about the other. So all four pairs are equally likely, and their sums are minus two, zero, zero and two.
adds/adds: The mean is still zero. Squared, the sums give four, zero, zero and four, which average to two: one plus one. The variances add.
adds/std: Standard deviations do not. Draw each as a square's side, with its variance as the area: the areas add to two, so the new side is the square root of two, about one point four one.
adds/fisher: That is why the square has a name of its own. In 1918, Ronald Fisher noted that independent causes add the squares of their standard deviations, and named that square the variance.
adds/prod: A unit's terms are products: say, a weight of minus two or two, times an independent input of minus one or one. Every product is minus two or two.
adds/mult: So the product's variance is four: the weight's four, times the input's one. With means of zero, variances multiply.
grow/n: Back to the unit's sum. Call its number of terms n.
grow/v: Make the terms independent, each with the same variance, v.
grow/var: Then their variances add, n times over: the variance of z is n times v, written var of z equals n v.
grow/big: The opening's hundred terms are each minus one or one, so v is one, and z has a variance of a hundred.
grow/ten: Its square root, ten, is the standard deviation: the wide swing we saw.
grow/root: Twenty-five terms give a standard deviation of five, and a hundred give ten. Four times the terms, twice the swing: it grows with the square root of n.
grow/unit: Now four hundred inputs of variance one, and weights with a standard deviation of zero point one.
grow/term: Squared, that is the weight's variance: zero point zero one. Times the input's one, each term's v is also zero point zero one.
grow/sum: Four hundred such terms add up to a variance of four.
grow/sd: And its square root, two, is the standard deviation of z.
